t: The Abbasids overthrew the Umayyads in 750 and ruled a multi-ethnic Islamic empire from their new capital, Baghdad.
Baghdad's House of Wisdom translated Greek, Persian and Indian learning into Arabic and helped give the world algebra.
Turkic slave soldiers, then Buyid and Seljuk overlords, hollowed out caliphal power long before the Mongols sacked Baghdad in 1258.
dyk: The word 'algebra' comes from al-jabr in the title of al-Khwarizmi's treatise on calculation, written in Abbasid Baghdad around 820.
ev: Abbasid rebels defeat the Umayyads at the Battle of the Great Zab
Al-Mansur founds the Round City of Baghdad on the Tigris
Al-Khwarizmi writes the treatise that gives algebra its name
Al-Mu'tasim moves the capital to Samarra to house his Turkic slave army
Assassination of al-Mutawakkil begins the Anarchy at Samarra
The Buyids take Baghdad, leaving the caliphs only religious authority
Hulagu Khan's Mongols sack Baghdad and execute Caliph al-Musta'sim
Selim I conquers Egypt, ending the Mamluk-sponsored shadow caliphate in Cairo
